sequence_description: I1 OIDC proof-integrity: attempt to inject unsigned request object (alg=none) at authorization endpoint; compare with a normal password login identity in same realm to ensure multi-identity coverage.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_alg_none_http_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_alg_none_http_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating missing proof verification (I1).

sequence_description: I1 issuer binding: compare default IdP config (no pinned issuer) vs pinned issuer config; attempt login with wrong Issuer to detect whether verification policy is applied to consumed Issuer semantics.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_wrong_issuer_default_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_wrong_issuer_default_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Default-config SAML IdP accepted assertion with arbitrary/untrusted Issuer (issuer validation skipped or misapplied).

sequence_description: I2 attack: replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after forcing a user-wide logout. Replay caches must not be cleared by session logout; second acceptance indicates replay protection scoped incorrectly to session state.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_attacker_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_attacker_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted a replayed SAML assertion ID after user logout; replay cache appears incorrectly scoped to session state.

sequence_description: I2 attack: verify baseline SAML login works, then submit an expired assertion (NotOnOrAfter 60 minutes in the past). Also perform a second valid login as a different identity to ensure multi-identity coverage and rule out global broker failure.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); expiry/freshness checks are not enforced.

sequence_description: Attempt to bypass SAML assertion replay detection by replaying the same Assertion/@ID across two different SAML IdP aliases within the same realm (tests whether replay cache is incorrectly scoped only per-provider alias). Includes two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_b_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_b_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML Assertion/@ID via a different IdP alias (replay cache scoped incorrectly)

sequence_description: Replay the same SAML Assertion/@ID after modifying the SAME IdP instance configuration (PUT) to test whether replay cache is incorrectly cleared/invalidated by config updates. Includes two identities and a config change + re-auth.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_after_change_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_after_change_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML Assertion/@ID after IdP config change (replay cache cleared by config update)

sequence_description: Test whether SAML assertion replay protection is incorrectly tied to realm/session token TTL settings: perform a successful SAML login, then change realm access token lifespan, then replay the exact same Assertion/@ID. Second acceptance would indicate replay cache invalidation or missing anti-replay enforcement after TTL-related config changes.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_replay_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_replay_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted replayed SAML assertion ID after realm TTL change (replay cache missing or incorrectly invalidated)

sequence_description: I3: Initiate OIDC auth (SP-initiated) then attempt to complete SAML login against a different provider alias than the one intended, simulating RelayState/InResponseTo swap across providers within the same realm.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_wrongprov_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_wrongprov_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML completion on a different provider alias than the initiating flow; indicates cross-provider flow splicing (RelayState/InResponseTo not bound to provider).

sequence_description: I5 attack: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, broker may grant permissions beyond upstream intent constraints.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SP accepted SAML assertion without <Conditions>, enabling authorization beyond upstream intent (no audience/time constraints).

sequence_description: I5: Attempt SAML login with missing Conditions (no audience/time bounds). Then harden broker config and re-attempt. If either attempt succeeds, Keycloak may mint sessions beyond upstream intent constraints; if hardening doesn't change outcome, policy may not be enforced.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_pre_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_pre_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML assertion without Conditions (no audience/time bounds) before hardening; may mint session beyond upstream intent.

sequence_description: I5: Attempt SAML login with missing Conditions (no audience/time bounds). Then harden broker config and re-attempt. If either attempt succeeds, Keycloak may mint sessions beyond upstream intent constraints; if hardening doesn't change outcome, policy may not be enforced.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_nocond_post_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_nocond_post_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML assertion without Conditions even after issuer pinning; broker policy may not bind authorization to upstream intent constraints.
